page.layout: One page of running text in a single block, with no marginal notes. Running head at the top. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: folet Antichristorum natura) maioribus molestius quàm alius quisquam, optimum grauabat princi-pem. Lubet hoc loco luculentissimum Hieronymi Marij testimonium assumere. Hic Pontifex, inquit, in Friderici odium, Lugduni concilium statim indi-xit: ubi illemet Innocentius concionabundus, Fridericum ipsum citabat. Friderici uero legatus, tempus opportunum dari precabatur, quo venire Lu-gdunum posset.

Quod Pontifex non modo non dedit: sed ira ac furore fuccensus, Fridericum anathe-mate notabat, imperiali dignitate priuabat, à iuramento fidelitatis principes absoluebat: eosq; ut alium eligant Imperatorem, hortabatur. Multa contra impissimum[?] Imperatorem falsa produxit: periurium, sacrilegium, & quorundam clericorum captiuitatem, atq; id genus alia. De quibus omnibus, etsi Imperator honestissimè apud principes antea se purgasset: Pontifex tamen adeò principes follicitauit, ac pollicitationibus commouit, ut Henricum Landgrauium Thuringiæ elegerint. Quod cùm ad imperatoris aures peruenisset, strenuè aduersus Innocentium, ac alios quoscunq; tyrannos, imperium suum defendit, donec in Apulia Pontificis laqueos effugere nequiuit.
Nam ibi quidam pontificia largitione corru-ptus, venenum sacro Imperatori exhibuit. Cuiu[?]

page.notes: The right-hand edge of the text is partly lost to a dark stain and the lower left is covered by a blue stain, so the lower-left corner is not affected. "impissimum" in the Latin is uncertain because the first letters are damaged; marked [?]. The final letter of "Cuius" is cut off at the right edge; marked [?]. The catchword "causa" is partly obscured by the stain and reads as printed. Line-end hyphens are kept where the printed hyphen is visible ("princi-pem", "indi-xit", "Lu-gdunum", "anathe-mate", "corru-ptus"); "Fride/ricum" and "ca/ptiuitatem" show no clear hyphen and are written whole.
